trigger_or_context: Something in the relationship is wrong or letting you down.
short_term_function: Waiting keeps the relationship going for now and lets you put off a hard choice.
developmental_cost: You make choices based on what you hope for, not on what is really happening.
adaptive_alternative_1: Look at what has really changed, not what you hope will change. Pick what you need to see, and by when. Then decide based on what really happened.
what_new_response_supports: You find out if things are really getting better or if you are only hoping.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: You may face a hard choice or a loss.
context_conditions: Waiting is fine if you can see real, steady change. It keeps the pattern going if it is only hope.
review_reason: Context-dependent: meaning turns on whether real change is visible; short-term function partly inferred from phase architecture.

trigger_or_context: The other person does something that lets you down or worries you.
short_term_function: Making excuses lets you keep seeing them in a good light instead of facing what they did.
developmental_cost: You judge them by the story you tell, not by what they really do.
adaptive_alternative_1: When you catch yourself explaining away what they did, name what actually happened first. Then decide what it means to you.
what_new_response_supports: You see their actions clearly, based on what really happened.
